And I know this is about as old as the internet itself, but relevant... Notes from an inexperienced Chili taster named Frank, who was visiting Texas from the East Coast:

Chili is a meat sauce. It was easy to prepare on the trail or in rustic settings. That said, the staple was dried beans. While many "purists" put forward that chili didn't have beans, they completely ignore that chili would traditionally be served with or over beans. So even bean-less chili would traditionally, commonly, be with beans. Of course, this means the chili would be thinner as it wouldn't have the bean's starches as a natural thickener.

Here's the rule. If chili is the primary entree, serve with beans. If the chili is only part of the main course and is to be served on top of other foods, such as eggs or hot dogs, then no beans.
